title: Maraudon
body: Maraudon lies beneath the Valley of Spears, the holy ground of the centaur, a tomb their people guard and only the most devout of them may enter. Its caverns run far down into the earth, and they are sick. A rot has spread through the upper caves: the water is poisoned, twisted vines and lashers choke the passages, oozes and larvae crawl through the damp, and satyrs move among them as if the place were theirs. Dryads walk there too, tending the poisoned growth as though it were still a garden. Deeper down the rot thins, and the stone itself is awake: elementals and giants of the earth walk halls of bare rock and crystal. Pale spirits of centaur drift through the caverns, paying the living no heed. Outsiders come all the same. Sisters of the Cenarion Circle in Desolace seek allies for a task they cannot finish alone, a dryad begs help for the family she left inside, an exile of the centaur wants something only these caverns hold, and scholars far away pay for its crystals.

title: Foulspore Cavern
body: Foulspore Cavern is a garden gone to rot under the stone. Great twisted vines rise from its floor, barbed lashers and constrictor vines wait for anything that passes, and creeping sludges ooze through the damp. Vile larvae swarm over the ground, and in one corner a spewer spits out still more of them. Dryads walk among the poisoned growth as though they still tended it, and some cry out that intruders do not belong in these gardens and that their bodies shall nourish the lovely creations growing there.

parts.body: Among the lashers of the cavern grew one far larger than the rest, Razorlash. It swept its foes with cleaving blows that struck several of them at once, and in the end it was cut down among the vines it had grown with.

title: The Wicked Grotto
body: The Wicked Grotto belongs to the satyrs. Putridus satyrs hold its passages, their breath foul with rot, and they strike low and gouge at those who face them, while tricksters slip behind their foes to stab them in the back and shadowstalkers creep about unseen. Poison sprites spit venom from a distance, and corruptors, demons of the rot, lay creeping corruption on all around them. Treants of the deep rot walk with them, stompers who shake the ground and tanglers wreathed in thorns.

title: Poison Falls
body: Poison Falls is where the fouled water of Maraudon comes down. It pours over the rock into pools crowded with noxious slimes, which loose clouds of poison on any who come near. Constrictor vines and barbed lashers grow thick along the water, and the lashers fling volleys of thorns. Sisters of Celebras, dryads of the caverns, hurl their spears from the banks, and cavern lurkers and shamblers of the deep knock intruders from their feet, the shamblers mending their own wounds as they fight. Satyrs and corruptors have come down here too, and the rot is as thick as anywhere in the caverns.

parts.body: Seldom found here is Meshlok the Harvester, a hulking bog beast who wanders the falls. Where he appeared he struck heavy blows and stamped the ground, stunning and hurling back those around him, until he was brought down beside the water.

title: The Deep Caverns
body: Below the rotting gardens Maraudon changes. The rot thins, the passages turn to bare rock and crystal, and what lives here belongs to the earth. Deep borers tunnel through the stone in swarms, and subterranean diemetradons stun intruders with bursts of piercing sound. Theradrim guardians, elementals of the deep rock, knock their foes down, and when one falls it breaks apart into shardlings that fight on. Primordial behemoths, giants of stone, hurl boulders and trample those who come close. No satyr walks here and no poisoned vine grows: the caverns are simply old, and their keepers want no visitors.

parts.body: Greatest of the giants in these caverns was Landslide. He struck his foes flying and trampled those beneath him, and as the fight wore on he shook the rock until those around him reeled, while shardlings of stone came pouring out of it to fight for him. When the giant fell at last, the shardlings he had called vanished with him.

title: Earth Song Falls
body: Deep in Maraudon the caverns open wide. Water falls from the heights into broad pools, and the rot of the upper caves has not reached here: green grows over the stone, frogs hop along the water's edge and fish move in the pools. Stolid snapjaws, turtles with spiked shells, crawl along the shores, and Thessala hydras rise from the water to lash at intruders with jets of water and poisoned bites. Whatever sickness fills the caves above, here the caverns are alive.

parts.body: The deep water beneath the falls hid Rotgrip, a crocolisk of enormous size who swam his round beneath the cliffs. He tore at his foes with bites that left them bleeding and drained their life to mend his own, but he was dragged down at last in his own water.

title: Princess Theradras
body: Princess Theradras walks the green valley deep in Maraudon, an enormous figure of living rock, and great giants of stone keep the valley about her. She is an elemental of the earth and a power in these caverns, and she says nothing at all to those who come before her. Of what she is and why she is here she gives no account; that is told elsewhere, in Desolace. Whoever reaches her valley meets her only as a foe.

parts.body: Theradras fought with the weight of the earth. She hurled boulders at her foes, shook the ground so that it flung away all around her, and roared at one foe until it stood paralyzed with terror while the rest fled from her in fear. In the end the princess fell in her valley. Then a spirit rose in the valley, a towering keeper of the grove, and he cried out that he was free, free from his bonds at last.

title: Celebras
body: Celebras the Cursed keeps to a hollow beside the poisoned falls, deep in Maraudon. He is a keeper of the grove, antlered and stag-bodied like the keepers of the Cenarion Circle, and dryads and twisted forces of nature gather about him. Whatever he was before, the corruption of the caverns has him now, and he turns on any who come near him. Those who face him here find only the curse.

parts.body: Celebras fought with the powers of his kind turned foul. He hurled bolts of nature's wrath, wrapped his foes in a storm of twisted tranquility that slowed them and wore them down, bound them in roots and called up corrupted forces of nature to fight for him. When he fell, the curse fell with him: there in his hollow stood Celebras again, calm now, the corruption gone from him.
sources: smart_scripts 12225 (Wrath 21807, Twisted Tranquility 21793, Corrupt Forces of Nature 21968, Entangling Roots 12747; on death summon 13716 Celebras the Redeemed at his place); not changed by the module
Spell.dbc 21793 (nature damage over time, slows movement and attacks), 21968 (summons Forces of Nature)

parts.body: Freed, Celebras speaks of what befell him. Long ago, he says, he and his dryad sisters came into these caves to free the tortured spirit of his uncle, Zaetar, but the corruption already spreading through the caverns overcame them, and they too fell, to wander the passages with toxins poisoning their minds. His spirit may be at rest now, but he knows he failed in his mission, and that sorrow he must bear.
sources: gossip_menu 5349 (npc_text 6354: At last, I am free of the corruption), option 0 to menu 5347 (npc_text 6380); no conditions

parts.body: Celebras is a son of Remulos. His father, he says, was strong and beautiful, his uncle Zaetar cunning and slight of build, and though the two were respected equally, Zaetar always felt he could never match his brother's glory. After Celebras and his sisters were born, Zaetar, blinded by jealousy, set out to outdo Remulos, and when he fell for a princess of elemental earth, Remulos knew the union was cursed and tried to stop him. Zaetar would not listen; he was the creator of his own end.
sources: gossip_menu 5349 options 1-2 to menus 5354 (npc_text 6181) and 5148 (npc_text 6180); no conditions
desolace.json 40535 part 1 (the union and the centaur's origin), pointed to

parts.body: Celebras's scepter was once his hope, and it gave him power over these caverns; with it he had meant to bring peace to his uncle's spirit. Now that its two pieces have come back to him, he needs help to make them one again: whoever aids him must follow him and do as he instructs while he channels the power to join the rod to the diamond.
sources: quest 7046 description and log (assist Celebras the Redeemed while he creates the Scepter of Celebras); QuestType 2, flags 2; starter and ender 13716; PrevQuestID 7044

parts.body: Celebras led his helpers to the place of the ritual, thanking them as he went: for so long he had drifted in his cursed form, and they had freed him. He set a tome before them, bade them read it and speak its words aloud, and began to channel, focusing on the stone. Together, he said, the two parts would become one again, and he spoke words in an old tongue. The scepter made, he gave it to them with a charge: its power must be used for good. Further on, he hoped, lay his uncle's remains, and much danger.

title: Lord Vyletongue
body: Lord Vyletongue is a satyr, master of the Putridus who hold the Wicked Grotto, and he keeps his seat at its heart with tricksters, shadowstalkers and deeprot treants close about him. He carries a bow as readily as a blade, and he does not wait for intruders to come within his reach before he strikes at them. He is the greatest of the satyrs in these caverns, and he treats the centaur's holy place as his own.

parts.body: Vyletongue fought from a distance whenever he could, loosing arrows at single foes and volleys that struck several at once. When they closed on him he threw down a smoke bomb that left those around him stunned and blinked away out of their reach. For all his tricks, the satyr lord fell at last in his own seat.

title: Noxxion
body: Noxxion is a great shape of poisoned water given life, and he waits at the far end of the Noxious Hollow, where the spore trees and the larvae are thickest. He looks like the sickness of the caverns given a body, and the Hollow around him is the foulest place in Maraudon. Whoever comes to the end of it finds him there, ready to drown them in his poison.

parts.body: Noxxion lashed his foes with volleys of poison and struck them off their feet with heavy blows. Beaten down to half his strength, he broke apart: five spawns of his substance poured out to fight, and Noxxion himself could not be reached until they were gone, when he drew himself together and fought on. In the end he fell in his Hollow.

title: Tinkerer Gizlock
body: Tinkerer Gizlock is a goblin, and what a goblin is doing in the deep caverns of the centaur's holy place, far below the rot and among the stone guardians and borers of the depths, he does not say. He has made a corner of the caverns his own, with his guns and gadgets about him, and he wants no one to know he is there. Anyone who stumbles on him has found something he meant to keep hidden.

parts.body: Gizlock met intruders shrieking that it was all his, that Gizlock was the ruler of this domain and they would never reveal his presence. He shot at them, lobbed bombs among them, set off flash bombs that sent any beasts with them running, and turned a goblin dragon gun on them that sprayed fire in a cone before him, when it did not blow up in his face. The ruler of his little domain fell all the same.

title: Zaetar's Spirit
body: When Princess Theradras fell, the spirit of Zaetar was freed, a towering keeper of the grove who stands now in the green valley where she walked. He does not mean to leave it. The centaur are his misbegotten sons and daughters, he says, and they have need of their father. This place rings with hope and with all that his father Cenarius preaches, and it sprang from him; he will not take that from them, not even for their crimes against him. He asks only one thing, to ease his brother's mind: that the first seed to fall from the life his remains nourished be carried to Remulos in Moonglade, with word that his spirit remains here and lives on.

title: The Spirits of the Khans
body: Ghosts walk the caverns of Maraudon. They are centaur, great khans by their look, and each bears the title of a khan of old, numbered as though in a line of rulers long gone. They drift through the rot and the dark, take no notice of the living who pass them and harm no one, and most who see them leave them be. Yet the dead of Maraudon are not beyond reach: there are those who know how to call them back into the world, and what is called back does not come in peace.

parts.body: The spirit of Maraudos, the Fourth Khan, paces the Wicked Grotto. Called into the world by one who knew the way, he took on a body again as Maraudos and turned on those who had summoned him. He fought as the khan he had been, until he fell a second time.

title: The Crystals of Maraudon
body: The crystals of Maraudon are wanted outside its caverns. More than one seeker who will not go in asks travelers to bring the stones out, and each says much the same thing in their own way: there is power in the crystals of Maraudon, power worth studying, and whoever carries some of it back will be paid for the trouble. What each of them means to make of that power, they keep largely to themselves. The asking is plain enough, and so is the promise of a reward.

parts.body: In Orgrimmar the troll mage Uthel'nay has heard that strong magics lie in the centaur holy place, and the tribes cannot stop him taking what he needs. He wants the purple crystals of the rock creatures made of shadowshard that dwell there, and he warns that the place is dangerous enough to bring friends.
sources: quest 7068 description (strong magics in the centaur holy place; the tribes protect it with their lives but cannot stop us; rock creatures made of shadowshard, the purple crystals; bring some friends); AllowableRaces 690; Uthel'nay 7311 in Orgrimmar

parts.body: The shadowshards suited Uthel'nay perfectly. Rituals of power and spells of great strength, he says, may come of such crystals, and he paid with a trinket of his making before turning back to his studies.
sources: quest 7068 completion text (rituals of power, spells of great strength) and reward text (perfect for me magics; take one of these trinkets; much studying)

parts.body: In Theramore, Archmage Tervosh has begun testing crystals for their arcane properties, and Lady Proudmoore has given him leave to ask travelers bound for Desolace to visit Maraudon. Within the ruined temple, he says, stand great elementals made of purplish stones, which he has named shadowshards, and he offers to fashion a trinket from any that are brought to him.
sources: quest 7070 description (testing crystals; Lady Proudmoore has given me leave; great elementals composed of purplish stones I've named shadowshards); AllowableRaces 1101; Tervosh 4967 in Theramore

parts.body: The shadowshards were just what Tervosh wanted. Others had already come back from Maraudon with samples, and from those he had fashioned his trinkets; he gave one in thanks and kept the new stones to study.
sources: quest 7070 reward text (other adventurers returned from there also; fashioned these; more samples to study)

parts.body: Willow of the Twilight's Hammer, at Kormek's Hut, names the place where the carvings lie: the crystal caverns of Terramok, deep within Maraudon to the west, an ancient place with much history, where relics of the old gods lie hidden behind the giant doors. Whoever braves the twisted evils of the caverns is to collect the theradric crystal carvings found there.
sources: quest 7028 description (the crystal caverns of Terramok lie to the west, deep within Maraudon; an ancient place with much history; relics of the old gods hidden behind the giant doors; theradric crystal carvings); QuestType 2, flags 8

parts.body: Willow laughed to see the carvings come back. Questions were not welcome, but the muttering that followed was plain enough: so easy to convince, and willing to do anything for the right price.
